producer_report.summary: Each job's admitted candidate is now pushed to `athena/ci/<job id>` on origin, and that branch is deleted when the job closes, whatever the outcome. The push happens in `check_and_verify` right before the early pull request. The delete sits in a new `finish_dispatched` wrapper, which runs after `close_dispatched` on the resume and produce-and-verify paths, including when the run ends in an error. The push goes through `gh::Remote`: it pushes when the branch is absent, does nothing when it already holds the commit, and replaces it, pinned to the head found, when a killed run left another commit. A failed push or delete is one warning line and does not change the outcome. With no https github.com origin (none, a local path, another host, or a look-alike URL) it pushes and deletes nothing, and emits one line: `ci         CI branch push is skipped because there is no GitHub origin`. The delete only fires if `remote_head` shows the branch. `Remote` gains `delete_branch` (default error; `GitRemote` runs `git push origin --delete refs/heads/<branch>`). `ci.yml` now runs on pushes to `main` and `athena/ci/**`, with a new comment; the 'fmt, clippy, tests' job is untouched. CHANGELOG has an entry saying nothing reads the CI result yet. New tests drive `Athena::go` through `early_seam` with the recording `EarlyFake` and never reach the network. The suite passed: 747 passed, 1 ignored (athena-core lib), plus the xtask tests and policy scan; fmt and clippy are clean. The integration tests of the other crates and the doctests did not run.

open_issues: `crates/athena-core/src/test_support.rs` is outside the brief's file list. I changed it as the plan said: `EarlyFake` now records and heads CI branches separately (`ci_calls`, `ci_head`, `fail_ci`, `fail_ci_delete`, `ci_of`, `delete_branch`). Without it the existing run_pin_tests assertions (one push, kinds [push, open_pr]) would break.
The push happens in `check_and_verify` after the disk gate, at the same spot as the early pull request, so a job held for low disk is not pushed until it is resumed.

The delete wrapper covers only the resume and produce-and-verify paths. Plan-stop closes, the blocked-landing retry and `athena close` make no delete, but none of them can follow a push that this job has not already deleted.

On the `athena/ci/**` push, the `history` job and the other required jobs also run, since only `attribution` is limited to main. The new comment says these runs are not on a pull request. I did not change which jobs run.
I did not run the full workspace `cargo test` (the other crates' integration tests and doctests); that is left to Athena's checks.
mistakes: My first real-git test asserted that deleting an already-missing branch fails. It does not for a local bare remote, so I removed the assertion.
I forgot the existing exact-line test in run/tests.rs and found it only when the suite failed. I updated it to expect the skip line.
learnings: `cargo test` accepts one name filter only, so several new tests need a shared prefix.

`git push origin --delete refs/heads/<missing>` to a local bare remote exits 0, so it is not an error. The delete is still guarded by `remote_head`, which skips a needless call and a network round trip.
One existing test counts every UI line from dispatch to landing (`a_fake_job_takes_its_baseline...`), so any new unconditional line in a no-origin run needs that test updated.
`early_seam` is thread-local and cfg(test) only, so the production `with_ci_remote` falls back to `GitRemote` over origin outside tests.
The gh/ module already has `ci_push_run_*` tests and ci_result.rs from the earlier work. They are unrelated and pass.
desires: A way to list which tests assert exact UI line counts, so a new always-emitted line could be checked in advance.
The first `cargo test -p athena-core` call returned only truncated output; a quiet mode in the brief's list would have found the failing test faster.
